greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ Αβραμ ἐτῶν ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα, καὶ ὤφθη κύριος τῷ Αβραμ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεός σου· εὐαρέστει ἐναντίον ἐμοῦ καὶ γίνου ἄμεμπτος,
hint: Abram at ninety-nine: the Lord appears — I am your God; be well pleasing before me and blameless.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾănî ʾēl šadday*, *I am El Shaddai*. The Greek has *I am your God*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *hithallēk lĕpānay*, *walk before me*. The Greek has *be well pleasing before me*, the verb it gives Enoch's walking at 5:22.
The present imperative of γίνομαι, with ἄμεμπτος, *not to be blamed, blameless*, for Hebrew *tāmîm*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Αβραμ]] of years ninety nine, and [[was seen|was seen, was looked at, was beheld and perceived and observed, was looked out for|ὁράω]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] to [[name:Αβραμ]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to him I am [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] of you; [[be well pleasing|be well pleasing, seem good, be resolved, be well pleased and satisfied|εὐαρεστέω]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of me and [[come into being|come to be, arise, be brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[not to be blamed|not to be blamed, blameless, perfect in its kind, without blame, not blaming and content|ἄμεμπτος]],

names.gloss: (Αβραμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrām, "the father is exalted")

greek: καὶ θήσομαι τὴν διαθήκην μου ἀνὰ μέσον ἐμοῦ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον σοῦ καὶ πληθυνῶ σε σφόδρα.
hint: I will set my covenant between me and you and multiply you greatly.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕʾettĕnâ*, *and I will give*. The Greek has θήσομαι, *I will set*, in the middle, rendered as the middle ἔθετο at 2:8.

reading: and [[I will set|I will set, I will put, I will place, I will plant, I will lay|τίθημι]] [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant|διαθήκη]] of me [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] of me and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] of you and [[I will make full|I will make full, I will increase, I will multiply|πληθύνω]] you [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]].

greek: καὶ ἔπεσεν Αβραμ ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς λέγων
hint: Abram falls on his face, and God speaks with him.

notes.text: πίπτω is first *to fall, fall down*; the pieces of its examples, *to fall in* the dust, *to fall by* another's hand, are left out.
λαλέω, the chain of GEN 12:4.

reading: and [[fell|fell, fell down, fell violently upon and attacked, threw himself down and fell down, fell and was ruined, fell and sank, fell short and failed, fell and turned out, was lucky, fell under and belonged to|πίπτω]] [[name:Αβραμ]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] of him, and [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] to him [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]]

greek: Καὶ ἐγὼ ἰδοὺ ἡ διαθήκη μου μετὰ σοῦ, καὶ ἔσῃ πατὴρ πλήθους ἐθνῶν.
hint: My covenant is with you: you will be father of a multitude of nations.

notes.text: Rahlfs opens the speech, and the verse, with a capital.
πλῆθος anarthrous, the chain of GEN 16:10 with the lexicon's own articles; πατήρ anarthrous, as at 9:18.

reading: And I [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant|διαθήκη]] of me [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] you, and you will be [[father|father, grandfather|πατήρ]] [[of a great number|of a great number and throng and crowd and multitude, of the greater number and greater part and mass and main body, of the majority and people, of the populace and mob, of quantity, of number, of magnitude and size, of extent, of amount, of length|πλῆθος]] [[of numbers of people accustomed to live together|of numbers of people accustomed to live together, of companies and bodies of men, of hosts, of swarms and flocks, of nations and peoples, of nations and gentiles, of special classes, of castes and tribes, of sexes|ἔθνος]].

greek: καὶ οὐ κληθήσεται ἔτι τὸ ὄνομά σου Αβραμ, ἀλλʼ ἔσται τὸ ὄνομά σου Αβρααμ, ὅτι πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε.
hint: No longer Abram: your name will be Abraham, for I have made you father of many nations.

notes.text: Paul quotes the clause letter for letter at Romans 4:17, καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε.
[[flag]] The Hebrew repeats *ʾab hămôn gôyim*, *father of a multitude of nations*, from 17:4. The Greek has πλήθους ἐθνῶν there and πολλῶν ἐθνῶν here, and the name's meaning is not in the Greek.
Two names, each glossed on its first occurrence.
The perfect of τίθημι: a standing state, `I have set and it stands set`.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone has Αβραμ before τὸ ὄνομά σου.

reading: and not [[will be called|will be called, will be summoned, will be invited|καλέω]] [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover|ἔτι]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of you [[name:Αβραμ]], [[otherwise|otherwise, but, except, yet, but then and however, but really and certainly|ἀλλά]] will be [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of you [[name:Αβρααμ]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[father|father, grandfather|πατήρ]] [[of many|of many, often, of much and mighty and great, of deep, of loud, of strong, of large and wide, of far, of long|πολύς]] [[of numbers of people accustomed to live together|of numbers of people accustomed to live together, of companies and bodies of men, of hosts, of swarms and flocks, of nations and peoples, of nations and gentiles, of special classes, of castes and tribes, of sexes|ἔθνος]] [[I have set|I have set and it stands set, I have put and it stands put, I have placed and it stands placed, I have planted and it stands planted, I have laid and it stands laid|τίθημι]] you.

names.gloss: (Αβρααμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrāhām, which the Hebrew of 17:5 hears in ʾab hămôn gôyim, "father of a multitude of nations")

greek: καὶ αὐξανῶ σε σφόδρα σφόδρα καὶ θήσω σε εἰς ἔθνη, καὶ βασιλεῖς ἐκ σοῦ ἐξελεύσονται.
hint: I will increase you greatly and make nations of you; kings will come from you.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕhiprētî*, *I will make fruitful*. The Greek has αὐξάνω, *to make large*, as at 1:22 for *pĕrû*.
[[flag]] The Berlin papyrus, 911, has the second σφόδρα; Codex Alexandrinus leaves it out.

reading: and [[I will make large|I will make large, I will increase and augment, I will increase in power and strengthen and exalt, I will promote to honour and glorify and magnify, I will grow and wax and increase, I will grow up|αὐξάνω]] you [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]] [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]] and [[I will set|I will set, I will put, I will place, I will plant, I will lay|τίθημι]] you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[numbers of people accustomed to live together|numbers of people accustomed to live together, companies and bodies of men, hosts, swarms and flocks, nations and peoples, nations and gentiles, special classes, castes and tribes, sexes|ἔθνος]], and [[kings|kings, chiefs, hereditary kings, lords and masters and householders, seconds of the nine archons, kings of Persia|βασιλεύς]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] you [[they will go out of|they will go out of, they will come out, they will go away and march off, they will go forth|ἐξέρχομαι]].

greek: καὶ στήσω τὴν διαθήκην μου ἀνὰ μέσον ἐμοῦ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον σοῦ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σπέρματός σου μετὰ σὲ εἰς γενεὰς αὐτῶν εἰς διαθήκην αἰώνιον εἶναί σου θεὸς καὶ τοῦ σπέρματός σου μετὰ σέ.
hint: An everlasting covenant with you and your seed after you: to be your God.

notes.text: θεός anarthrous, the predicate after εἶναι, not fronted: qualitative, as CLAUDE.md sets it out. σου is the genitive, *to be of you God*, for Hebrew *lĕkā*.
ἵστημι, the chain of GEN 6:18.

reading: and [[I will make to stand|I will make to stand, I will set, I will stop and stay and check, I will set up and raise, I will establish and institute, I will appoint, I will weigh|ἵστημι]] [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant|διαθήκη]] of me [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] of me and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] of you and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] [[of that which is sown|of that which is sown, of the seed, of the germ and origin and element, of the offspring and issue, of the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[races|races, stocks and families, breeds, tribes and nations, generations, offspring, birth-places, ages and times of life|γενεά]] of them [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[a disposition|a disposition of property by will, a will and testament, an arrangement between two parties, a covenant|διαθήκη]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting, eternal|αἰώνιος]] to be of you [[God|everything that God is by nature, deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]] and [[of that which is sown|of that which is sown, of the seed, of the germ and origin and element, of the offspring and issue, of the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] you.

greek: καὶ δώσω σοι καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου μετὰ σὲ τὴν γῆν, ἣν παροικεῖς, πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν Χανααν, εἰς κατάσχεσιν αἰώνιον καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτοῖς θεός. —
hint: I will give you and your seed the land where you sojourn, all Canaan, for an everlasting possession.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾēt ʾereṣ mĕgurêkā*, *the land of your sojournings*. The Greek has *the land which you dwell beside*.

κατάσχεσις has no Middle Liddell entry; LSJ is first *holding back, restraining, retention*, then *possession*. Stephen's speech has the phrase of this promise, Acts 7:5, δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτήν.
θεός anarthrous, the predicate, not fronted, as at 17:7.
Rahlfs prints a dash after the verse, closing a section.

reading: and [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to you and [[to that which is sown|to that which is sown, to the seed, to the germ and origin and element, to the offspring and issue, to the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] you [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]], which [[you dwell beside|you dwell beside, you dwell along the coast of, you live near, you dwell among, you lie near, you live in and sojourn|παροικέω]], [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] [[name:Χανααν]], [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[holding back|holding back, restraining, retention, possession, relation and attitude|κατάσχεσις]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting, eternal|αἰώνιος]] and I will be to them [[God|everything that God is by nature, deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]].

names.gloss: (Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Αβρααμ Σὺ δὲ τὴν διαθήκην μου διατηρήσεις, σὺ καὶ τὸ σπέρμα σου μετὰ σὲ εἰς τὰς γενεὰς αὐτῶν.
hint: You and your seed after you shall keep my covenant.

notes.text: διατηρέω is first *to watch closely, observe*; *to keep faithfully* is its second.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] you [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant|διαθήκη]] of me [[you will watch closely|you will watch closely, you will observe, you will keep faithfully and maintain, you will keep|διατηρέω]], you and [[that which is sown|that which is sown, the seed, the germ and origin and element, the offspring and issue, the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the races|the races, the stocks and families, the breeds, the tribes and nations, the generations, the offspring, the birth-places, the ages and times of life|γενεά]] of them.

greek: καὶ αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη, ἣν διατηρήσεις, ἀνὰ μέσον ἐμοῦ καὶ ὑμῶν καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σπέρματός σου μετὰ σὲ εἰς τὰς γενεὰς αὐτῶν· περιτμηθήσεται ὑμῶν πᾶν ἀρσενικόν,
hint: This is the covenant: every male among you shall be circumcised.

notes.lemma: ἣν διατηρήσεις … εἰς τὰς γενεὰς αὐτῶν
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾăšer tišmĕrû*, *which you (plural) shall keep*, and has no *for their generations*. The Greek has the singular, and the phrase of 17:9.

περιτέμνω is first *to cut* or *clip round about*: the passive takes the active's senses and its own, *to be curtailed of*, *to be cut off, intercepted*, last. *They practise circumcision* is a translation of the middle alone, and no passive form takes it.
Middle Liddell heads it ἀρρενικός, one translation, *male*: plain text.

reading: and [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant|διαθήκη]], which [[you will watch closely|you will watch closely, you will observe, you will keep faithfully and maintain, you will keep|διατηρέω]], [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] of me and of you and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] [[of that which is sown|of that which is sown, of the seed, of the germ and origin and element, of the offspring and issue, of the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of you [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the races|the races, the stocks and families, the breeds, the tribes and nations, the generations, the offspring, the birth-places, the ages and times of life|γενεά]] of them; [[will be cut|will be cut, will be clipped round about, will be pruned, will be cut off, will be cut off and hemmed in all round, will be curtailed of, will be cut off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]] of you [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] male,

greek: καὶ περιτμηθήσεσθε τὴν σάρκα τῆς ἀκροβυστίας ὑμῶν, καὶ ἔσται ἐν σημείῳ διαθήκης ἀνὰ μέσον ἐμοῦ καὶ ὑμῶν.
hint: You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, a sign of the covenant.

notes.text: The passive with an accusative of the part, *you will be cut as to the flesh*.
ἀκροβυστία is first *the foreskin*; Middle Liddell's second is *circumcision*, its collective *the uncircumcision, the uncircumcised*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *lĕʾôt bĕrît*, *for a sign of a covenant*. The Greek has ἐν. Paul has σημεῖον ἔλαβεν περιτομῆς at Romans 4:11.

reading: and [[you will be cut|you will be cut, you will be clipped round about, you will be pruned, you will be cut off, you will be cut off and hemmed in all round, you will be curtailed of, you will be cut off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]] [[the flesh|the flesh, the muscles, the body, man's nature generally|σάρξ]] [[of the foreskin|of the foreskin, of the circumcision, of the uncircumcision, of the uncircumcised|ἀκροβυστία]] of you, and will be [[in sign|within, inside of, and by means of sign, mark and token, sign from the gods and omen, signal, standard and ensign, boundary|ἐν; σημεῖον]] [[of a disposition|of a disposition of property by will, of a will and testament, of an arrangement between two parties, of a covenant|διαθήκη]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] of me and of you.

greek: καὶ παιδίον ὀκτὼ ἡμερῶν περιτμηθήσεται ὑμῖν πᾶν ἀρσενικὸν εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν, ὁ οἰκογενὴς τῆς οἰκίας σου καὶ ὁ ἀργυρώνητος ἀπὸ παντὸς υἱοῦ ἀλλοτρίου, ὃς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματός σου.
hint: Every male child of eight days, homeborn or bought from a foreigner, shall be circumcised.

notes.text: Middle Liddell's *a little* or *young child*, tagged in two pieces: *a little* is not a gloss by itself, and *young child* heads.
Luke 1:59 has ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἦλθον περιτεμεῖν τὸ παιδίον, and Paul περιτομῇ ὀκταήμερος, Philippians 3:5.
ἀλλότριος is first *of* or *belonging to another*: *of* is not a gloss by itself, and *belonging to another* heads.
ἀργυρώνητος, one translation, *bought with silver*: plain text.

greek: περιτομῇ περιτμηθήσεται ὁ οἰκογενὴς τῆς οἰκίας σου καὶ ὁ ἀργυρώνητος, καὶ ἔσται ἡ διαθήκη μου ἐπὶ τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν εἰς διαθήκην αἰώνιον.
hint: Homeborn and bought alike must be circumcised; my covenant will be in your flesh.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew doubles the verb, *himmôl yimmôl*, infinitive and finite. The Greek has the noun in the dative, *to circumcision*, with the verb.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *miqnat kaspekā*, *bought with your silver*. The Greek has no *your*.
περιτομή, one translation, *circumcision*: plain text.

reading: to circumcision [[will be cut|will be cut, will be clipped round about, will be pruned, will be cut off, will be cut off and hemmed in all round, will be curtailed of, will be cut off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]] [[the born in the house|the born in the house, the homebred|οἰκογενής]] [[of the building|of the building, of the house, of the dwelling, of the household and domestic establishment, of the household and inmates of the house, of the house and family from which one is descended|οἰκία]] of you and the bought with silver, and will be [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant|διαθήκη]] of me [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the flesh|of the flesh, of the muscles, of the body, of man's nature generally|σάρξ]] of you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[a disposition|a disposition of property by will, a will and testament, an arrangement between two parties, a covenant|διαθήκη]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting, eternal|αἰώνιος]].

greek: καὶ ἀπερίτμητος ἄρσην, ὃς οὐ περιτμηθήσεται τὴν σάρκα τῆς ἀκροβυστίας αὐτοῦ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ, ἐξολεθρευθήσεται ἡ ψυχὴ ἐκείνη ἐκ τοῦ γένους αὐτῆς, ὅτι τὴν διαθήκην μου διεσκέδασεν.
hint: The uncircumcised male, not circumcised on the eighth day, shall be destroyed from his people.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾet-bĕrîtî hēpar*, *he has broken my covenant*, with no conjunction. The Greek has ὅτι and *scattered abroad*.
ἐξολεθρεύω, spelled as MorphGNT has it at Acts 3:23; Middle Liddell heads it ἐξολοθρεύω, one translation, *to destroy utterly*: plain text.
ψυχή, the chain of GEN 2:7; αὐτῆς agrees with it.
One translation, *uncircumcised*: plain text; so ὄγδοος, *eighth*.

greek: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς τῷ Αβρααμ Σαρα ἡ γυνή σου, οὐ κληθήσεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς Σαρα, ἀλλὰ Σαρρα ἔσται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς.
hint: Sarai your wife will no longer be called Sarai; Sarah will be her name.

notes.text: Two names, each glossed on its first occurrence.
ἀλλά, the chain of GEN 15:4, for Hebrew *kî*.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] to [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[name:Σαρα]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of you, not [[will be called|will be called, will be summoned, will be invited|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of her [[name:Σαρα]], [[otherwise|otherwise, but, except, yet, but then and however, but really and certainly|ἀλλά]] [[name:Σαρρα]] will be [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of her.

names.gloss: (Σαρα, from Hebrew Śāray, usually connected with śārâ, "princess")

greek: εὐλογήσω δὲ αὐτὴν καὶ δώσω σοι ἐξ αὐτῆς τέκνον· καὶ εὐλογήσω αὐτόν, καὶ ἔσται εἰς ἔθνη, καὶ βασιλεῖς ἐθνῶν ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔσονται.
hint: I will bless her and give you a child by her; nations and kings will come from him.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bēn*, *a son*. The Greek has τέκνον, *that which is borne*.

[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ûbēraktîhā wĕhāyĕtâ lĕgôyim malkê ʿammîm mimmennâ yihyû*, *I will bless her, and she shall become nations; kings of peoples shall be from her*. The Greek has the masculine, of the child: *him*, *from him*.

reading: [[I will speak well of|I will speak well of, I will praise, I will honour, I will bless|εὐλογέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], her and [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to you [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] her [[that which is borne|that which is borne, the born, a child, my son and my child, the young|τέκνον]]; and [[I will speak well of|I will speak well of, I will praise, I will honour, I will bless|εὐλογέω]] him, and will be [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[numbers of people accustomed to live together|numbers of people accustomed to live together, companies and bodies of men, hosts, swarms and flocks, nations and peoples, nations and gentiles, special classes, castes and tribes, sexes|ἔθνος]], and [[kings|kings, chiefs, hereditary kings, lords and masters and householders, seconds of the nine archons, kings of Persia|βασιλεύς]] [[of numbers of people accustomed to live together|of numbers of people accustomed to live together, of companies and bodies of men, of hosts, of swarms and flocks, of nations and peoples, of nations and gentiles, of special classes, of castes and tribes, of sexes|ἔθνος]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] him will be.

greek: καὶ ἔπεσεν Αβρααμ ἐπὶ πρόσωπον καὶ ἐγέλασεν καὶ εἶπεν ἐν τῇ διανοίᾳ αὐτοῦ λέγων Εἰ τῷ ἑκατονταετεῖ γενήσεται, καὶ εἰ Σαρρα ἐνενήκοντα ἐτῶν οὖσα τέξεται;
hint: Abraham falls on his face and laughs: shall a hundred-year-old have a child, and Sarah bear at ninety?

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿal-pānāyw*, *on his face*, as at 17:3. The Greek has no αὐτοῦ.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕlibbô*, *in his heart*. The Greek has *in his thought*.
The verb in the Hebrew, *wayyiṣḥāq*, is the one the name Ισαακ holds; the Greek has γελάω, and the name as a transliteration.
ἑκατονταέτης has no Middle Liddell entry; LSJ's one sense is *of a hundred years*, *years old*, citing this verse. Paul has ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων of Abraham, Romans 4:19.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds υἱός; most witnesses do not.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[fell|fell, fell down, fell violently upon and attacked, threw himself down and fell down, fell and was ruined, fell and sank, fell short and failed, fell and turned out, was lucky, fell under and belonged to|πίπτω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] and [[laughed|laughed, laughed at, derided|γελάω]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[in the thought|within, inside of, and by means of the thought, the intention and purpose, the notion and opinion, the intelligence and understanding, the meaning|ἐν; διάνοια]] of him [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[if|if, whether, come on|εἰ]] [[to the of a hundred years|to the of a hundred years, to the years old|ἑκατονταετής]] [[will come into being|will come to be, will arise, will be brought into existence|γίνομαι]], and [[if|if, whether, come on|εἰ]] [[name:Σαρρα]] ninety of years being [[will bring into the world|will bring into the world, will bear, will bring forth, will beget, will produce and yield|τίκτω]]?

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Αβρααμ πρὸς τὸν θεόν Ισμαηλ οὗτος ζήτω ἐναντίον σου.
hint: Abraham: may Ishmael live before you.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *lû yišmāʿēʾl yiḥyeh*, *O that Ishmael might live*. The Greek has *this Ishmael, let him live*.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[name:Ισμαηλ]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[let live|let live, let be in full life and strength, let be fresh and strong|ζάω]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of you.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς τῷ Αβρααμ Ναί· ἰδοὺ Σαρρα ἡ γυνή σου τέξεταί σοι υἱόν, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ισαακ, καὶ στήσω τὴν διαθήκην μου πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰς διαθήκην αἰώνιον καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτόν.
hint: Yes: Sarah will bear you a son, Isaac, and my covenant will stand with him.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾăbāl*, *truly* or *no, but*. The Greek has *yea*.
Middle Liddell is first *yea, verily*; *aye, yes* in answers last.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads πρὸς Αβρααμ; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has τῷ.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] to [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[yea|yea, verily, aye and yes|ναί]]; [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[name:Σαρρα]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of you [[will bring into the world|will bring into the world, will bear, will bring forth, will beget, will produce and yield|τίκτω]] to you a son, and [[you will call|you will call, you will summon, you will call to yourself, you will invite|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of him [[name:Ισαακ]], and [[I will make to stand|I will make to stand, I will set, I will stop and stay and check, I will set up and raise, I will establish and institute, I will appoint, I will weigh|ἵστημι]] [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant|διαθήκη]] of me [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] him [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[a disposition|a disposition of property by will, a will and testament, an arrangement between two parties, a covenant|διαθήκη]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting, eternal|αἰώνιος]] and [[to that which is sown|to that which is sown, to the seed, to the germ and origin and element, to the offspring and issue, to the race and descent|σπέρμα]] of him [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] him.

greek: περὶ δὲ Ισμαηλ ἰδοὺ ἐπήκουσά σου· ἰδοὺ εὐλόγησα αὐτὸν καὶ αὐξανῶ αὐτὸν καὶ πληθυνῶ αὐτὸν σφόδρα· δώδεκα ἔθνη γεννήσει, καὶ δώσω αὐτὸν εἰς ἔθνος μέγα.
hint: As for Ishmael, I have heard you: he will father twelve nations.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bimʾōd mĕʾōd*, doubled, as at 17:2 and 17:6. The Greek has σφόδρα once.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *šĕnêm-ʿāśār nĕśîʾim*, *twelve princes*. The Greek has *twelve nations*.
περί with the genitive, the chain of GEN 12:17.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads καί for this second ἰδού; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has ἰδού.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[round about|round about, around, about and near, about and for and on account of, about and concerning, for very|περί + genitive]] [[name:Ισμαηλ]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[I listened|I listened, I hearkened to and heard, I gave ear and hearkened, I obeyed|ἐπακούω]] of you; [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[I spoke well of|I spoke well of, I praised, I honoured, I blessed|εὐλογέω]] him and [[I will make large|I will make large, I will increase and augment, I will increase in power and strengthen and exalt, I will promote to honour and glorify and magnify, I will grow and wax and increase, I will grow up|αὐξάνω]] him and [[I will make full|I will make full, I will increase, I will multiply|πληθύνω]] him [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]]; twelve [[numbers of people accustomed to live together|numbers of people accustomed to live together, companies and bodies of men, hosts, swarms and flocks, nations and peoples, nations and gentiles, special classes, castes and tribes, sexes|ἔθνος]] [[will beget|will beget, will engender, will bring forth, will produce|γεννάω]], and [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] him [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[a number of people accustomed to live together|a number of people accustomed to live together, a company and body of men, a host, swarms and flocks, a nation and people, the nations and gentiles, a special class, a caste and tribe, a sex|ἔθνος]] [[big|big, great, tall, full-grown, vast and high, spacious and wide, strong and mighty, violent, loud, prevailing, weighty and important|μέγας]].

greek: τὴν δὲ διαθήκην μου στήσω πρὸς Ισαακ, ὃν τέξεταί σοι Σαρρα εἰς τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐν τῷ ἐνιαυτῷ τῷ ἑτέρῳ.
hint: But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear at this time next year.

notes.text: ἐνιαυτός is first *any long period of time, a cycle, period*; with the article, *the* stands where the lexicon has *any*, as it does for *a*. *A year* is its second sense.
The repeated article before the adjective, plain `the`, as at 14:18.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant|διαθήκη]] of me [[I will make to stand|I will make to stand, I will set, I will stop and stay and check, I will set up and raise, I will establish and institute, I will appoint, I will weigh|ἵστημι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Ισαακ]], whom [[will bring into the world|will bring into the world, will bear, will bring forth, will beget, will produce and yield|τίκτω]] to you [[name:Σαρρα]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the due measure|the due measure, the proportion, the fitness, the vital part, the right point of time, the proper time and season, the exact and critical time, the time, the advantage and profit and fruit|καιρός]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[in the long period of time|within, inside of, and by means of the long period of time, the cycle, the period, the year|ἐν; ἐνιαυτός]] the [[other|other, one of two, the other of two, another, second, different, other than, worse|ἕτερος]].

greek: συνετέλεσεν δὲ λαλῶν πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἀνέβη ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ Αβρααμ.
hint: God finishes speaking with him and goes up from Abraham.

notes.text: συντελέω with the participle, *finished talking*; the chain of GEN 2:2.

reading: [[brought quite to an end|brought quite to an end, completed, accomplished, made up into the whole and into the number|συντελέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[talking|talking, chatting, prattling, babbling, saying, talking of, speaking, chattering, chirping|λαλέω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] him and [[went up|went up, mounted, went up to, embarked|ἀναβαίνω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[name:Αβρααμ]].

greek: Καὶ ἔλαβεν Αβρααμ Ισμαηλ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντας τοὺς οἰκογενεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀργυρωνήτους καὶ πᾶν ἄρσεν τῶν ἀνδρῶν τῶν ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ Αβρααμ καὶ περιέτεμεν τὰς ἀκροβυστίας αὐτῶν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης, καθὰ ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεός.
hint: That same day Abraham circumcises Ishmael and every male of his house.

notes.lemma: ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʿeṣem hayyôm hazzeh*, *in the very bone of this day*. The Greek has *in the time of that day*.
The repeated article before the phrase, plain `the`.
The accusative plural, *the foreskins*, where ἀκροβυστίας at 17:11 is the genitive singular.

reading: And [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[name:Ισμαηλ]] the son of him and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the born in the house|the born in the house, the homebred|οἰκογενής]] of him and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] the bought with silver and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[male|male, the male sex, masculine and strong, mighty|ἄρσην]] [[of the men|of the men, of the men in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] the [[in the house|within, inside of, and by means of the house, the abode and dwelling, the room and chamber, the house of a god and temple, the household goods and substance, the household and family|ἐν; οἶκος]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] and [[cut|cut, clipped round about, pruned, cut off, cut off and hemmed in all round|περιτέμνω]] [[the foreskins|the foreskins, the circumcisions, the uncircumcisions, the uncircumcised|ἀκροβυστία]] of them [[in the due measure|within, inside of, and by means of the due measure, the proportion, the fitness, the vital part, the right point of time, the proper time and season, the exact and critical time, the time, the advantage and profit and fruit|ἐν; καιρός]] [[of the day|of the day, of the day-break, of the time|ἡμέρα]] [[of that|of that, of the one there, of the more remote|ἐκεῖνος]], [[according as|according as, just as, like as if, exactly as|καθά]] [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] to him [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]].

greek: Αβρααμ δὲ ἦν ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐτῶν, ἡνίκα περιέτεμεν τὴν σάρκα τῆς ἀκροβυστίας αὐτοῦ·
hint: Abraham is ninety-nine when he is circumcised.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕhimmōlô*, *in his being circumcised*. The Greek has the active, *he cut*.
εἰμί of age, the state formula of GEN 1:2 in full, as at 16:16.

reading: [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, ninety nine of years, [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever|ἡνίκα]] [[cut|cut, clipped round about, pruned, cut off, cut off and hemmed in all round|περιτέμνω]] [[the flesh|the flesh, the muscles, the body, man's nature generally|σάρξ]] [[of the foreskin|of the foreskin, of the circumcision, of the uncircumcision, of the uncircumcised|ἀκροβυστία]] of him;

greek: Ισμαηλ δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἐτῶν δέκα τριῶν ἦν, ἡνίκα περιετμήθη τὴν σάρκα τῆς ἀκροβυστίας αὐτοῦ.
hint: Ishmael is thirteen when he is circumcised.

notes.text: εἰμί of age, the state formula in full, after the numbers as the Greek has it.

reading: [[name:Ισμαηλ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], the son of him of years ten three was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever|ἡνίκα]] [[was cut|was cut, was clipped round about, was pruned, was cut off, was cut off and hemmed in all round, was curtailed of, was cut off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]] [[the flesh|the flesh, the muscles, the body, man's nature generally|σάρξ]] [[of the foreskin|of the foreskin, of the circumcision, of the uncircumcision, of the uncircumcised|ἀκροβυστία]] of him.

greek: ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης περιετμήθη Αβρααμ καὶ Ισμαηλ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ·
hint: On that same day Abraham and Ishmael are circumcised.

notes.text: The aorist passive, singular with two subjects, as the Hebrew *nimmôl*.

reading: [[in the due measure|within, inside of, and by means of the due measure, the proportion, the fitness, the vital part, the right point of time, the proper time and season, the exact and critical time, the time, the advantage and profit and fruit|ἐν; καιρός]] [[of the day|of the day, of the day-break, of the time|ἡμέρα]] [[of that|of that, of the one there, of the more remote|ἐκεῖνος]] [[was cut|was cut, was clipped round about, was pruned, was cut off, was cut off and hemmed in all round, was curtailed of, was cut off and intercepted|περιτέμνω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] and [[name:Ισμαηλ]] the son of him;

greek: καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ οἰκογενεῖς καὶ οἱ ἀργυρώνητοι ἐξ ἀλλογενῶν ἐθνῶν, περιέτεμεν αὐτούς.
hint: All the men of his house, homeborn and bought from foreigners, he circumcised.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *nimmōlû ʾittô*, *were circumcised with him*. The Greek has *he cut them*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *mēʾēt ben-nēkār*, *from a foreigner*. The Greek has *from nations of another race*.
ἀλλογενής, one sense, *of another race, a stranger*, in the genitive plural: the case's `of` stands before the lexicon's own.

reading: and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the men|the men, the men in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] [[of the house|of the house, of the abode and dwelling, of the room and chamber, of the house of a god and temple, of the household goods and substance, of the household and family|οἶκος]] of him and [[the born in the house|the born in the house, the homebred|οἰκογενής]] and the bought with silver [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of of another race|of of another race, of strangers|ἀλλογενής]] [[of numbers of people accustomed to live together|of numbers of people accustomed to live together, of companies and bodies of men, of hosts, of swarms and flocks, of nations and peoples, of nations and gentiles, of special classes, of castes and tribes, of sexes|ἔθνος]], [[cut|cut, clipped round about, pruned, cut off, cut off and hemmed in all round|περιτέμνω]] them.
